Chaneka writes down an array aaa of nnn positive integer elements. Initially, all elements are not circled. In one operation, Chaneka can circle an element. It is possible to circle the same element more than once.

After doing all operations, Chaneka makes a sequence rrr consisting of all uncircled elements of aaa following the order of their indices.

Chaneka also makes another sequence ppp such that its length is equal to the number of operations performed and pip_ipi​ is the index of the element that is circled in the iii-th operation.

Chaneka wants to do several operations such that sequence rrr is equal to sequence ppp. Help her achieve this, or report if it is impossible! Note that if there are multiple solutions, you can print any of them.

Input

The first line contains a single integer nnn (1≤n≤2⋅1051 \leq n \leq 2\cdot10^51≤n≤2⋅105) — the size of array aaa.

The second line contains nnn integers a1,a2,a3,…,ana_1,a_2,a_3,\ldots,a_na1​,a2​,a3​,…,an​ (1≤ai≤n1\leq a_i\leq n1≤ai​≤n).

Output

A single line containing −1-1−1 if it is impossible.

Otherwise, the output consists of two lines. The first line contains an integer zzz representing the number of operations performed. The second line contains zzz integers, the iii-th integer represents the index of the element circled in the iii-th operation. If there are multiple solutions, you can print any of them.

Examples

InputCopiar OutputCopiar 
5
3 4 2 2 3

3
3 2 3
InputCopiar OutputCopiar 
3
1 2 3

-1

Note

In the first example, doing the operations like the example output gives the following results:

  • Element a2a_2a2​ gets circled 111 time.
  • Element a3a_3a3​ gets circled 222 times.
  • The uncircled elements (ordered by their indices) are a1a_1a1​, a4a_4a4​, and a5a_5a5​. So r=[3,2,3]r=[3,2,3]r=[3,2,3].
  • p=[3,2,3]p=[3,2,3]p=[3,2,3]

Therefore, r=pr=pr=p.

In the second example, it is impossible.
